name: Vesugen
summary: A Lys-Glu-Asp tripeptide (KED) from Khavinson's lab pitched for blood vessels; cell-culture data, one small Russian human report, no appearance link.
lead: Vesugen is a synthetic tripeptide, Lys-Glu-Asp (KED, also called T-38), developed by Vladimir Khavinson's group and described as a vasoprotective peptide based on sequences from vascular-tissue extracts .

name: Crystagen
summary: A Russian three-amino-acid 'bioregulator' peptide with spleen and immune claims backed only by small lab reports.
lead: Crystagen is a short synthetic peptide with the sequence Thr-Lys-Glu (TKE, also written EDP in some listings), one of the "Khavinson peptides" developed in Russia as so-called peptide bioregulators. It is described in the literature as an immunoprotective peptide whose reported actions concern the spleen and the immune system during ageing.

name: Chonluten
summary: A tripeptide from the Khavinson 'bioregulator' family said to support respiratory mucosa, with only cell-line data.
lead: Chonluten is a short synthetic peptide with the sequence Glu-Asp-Gly (EDG), one of the Khavinson peptides that are marketed under the term peptide bioregulators. It is described as a regulator of the respiratory mucosa.

name: Livagen
summary: A Russian four-amino-acid 'bioregulator' peptide with lab data on old-donor chromatin and no human appearance data.
lead: Livagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the sequence Lys-Glu-Asp-Ala (KEDA), developed in Russia as one of the short peptide bioregulators associated with Vladimir Khavinson and the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology.
claims: Livagen makes cells look and act younger by turning on youthful genes
Peptide bioregulators are among the few useful non-injectables for looksmaxxers

name: Thymalin
summary: A Russian calf-thymus peptide extract sold as an immune and longevity drug, with data mostly from its developers.
lead: Thymalin is a Russian pharmaceutical preparation made by mild acid extraction of calf thymus. It was put into practice there as an immunocorrector, a drug meant to modulate immune function.

name: Epithalamin
summary: The bovine pineal extract behind Epitalon, with lifespan data in flies and rodents but no human trials.
lead: Epithalamin is a peptide preparation extracted from the pineal gland of cattle, developed by Vladimir Khavinson's group in Russia. The synthetic tetrapeptide Epitalon was later derived from it.

name: Cortexin
summary: A Russian cattle-brain peptide injection used for neurological conditions, with some local trials and no appearance data.
lead: Cortexin is a neuroprotective peptide medicine made by the Russian company Geropharm from the cerebral cortex of cattle. It is given by intramuscular injection and used mainly in Russia and some post-Soviet countries for neurological conditions such as cerebrovascular disorders, head injury effects, encephalopathies and developmental delay in children.

name: Retinalamin
summary: Animal-derived retinal peptide extract from Russia, studied in glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy; no appearance use is documented.
lead: Retinalamin is a polypeptide extract prepared from the retinas of cattle or pigs. It was developed in Russia within the group of gerontologist Vladimir Khavinson and belongs to the family of animal-tissue-derived peptide preparations that this group calls cytomedins or peptide bioregulators . It is used clinically in Russia and neighbouring countries, mainly by injection, for retinal conditions such as glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy .

name: Prostatilen
summary: Bovine prostate peptide extract used in post-Soviet urology; mostly Russian-language data and no appearance use.
lead: Prostatilen is a peptide preparation extracted from the prostate glands of cattle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the mid-1980s and has been used in Russia, Ukraine and other post-Soviet countries for chronic prostatitis and benign prostatic hyperplasia, according to Grokipedia . It belongs to the family of organ-derived peptide bioregulators, or cytomedins, associated with Vladimir Khavinson's research group .

name: Cortagen
summary: Khavinson brain-derived tetrapeptide (AEDP) studied only in cells and animals; no appearance evidence.
lead: Cortagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the sequence Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro, made by Vladimir Khavinson's group in Russia from the amino-acid analysis of Cortexin, a natural brain-cortex peptide preparation . It is one of the short synthetic peptide bioregulators the group proposes as tissue-specific regulators of ageing-related changes .

name: Ovagen
summary: Khavinson liver-targeted tripeptide (EDL) with essentially no verifiable published human data and no appearance use.
lead: Ovagen is a synthetic tripeptide with the sequence Glu-Asp-Leu (EDL), developed by Vladimir Khavinson's group in Russia as part of its Cytogen family of short peptides, according to Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia . It is described there as investigated for effects on the liver and gastrointestinal tract and as modulating gene expression in a tissue-specific way .

name: Pancragen
summary: Khavinson pancreas-targeted tetrapeptide with cell, animal and one small human study; no appearance evidence.
lead: Pancragen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Trp, usually amidated) developed by Vladimir Khavinson and colleagues at the Saint Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology, designed to target pancreatic tissue . It belongs to the short synthetic peptide bioregulators the group proposes as tissue-specific regulators in ageing .

name: Prostamax
summary: A four-amino-acid Russian "bioregulator" peptide tied to prostate support; only cell and rat-tissue work exists.
lead: Prostamax is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the sequence Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro (KEDP), developed by Russian gerontologist Vladimir Khavinson and colleagues at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology as one of a series of short-peptide "bioregulators" . It was designed around the amino acid composition of Prostatilen, a prostate-tissue extract preparation, and is described by its developers as acting on prostate tissue .

name: Testagen
summary: A four-amino-acid "bioregulator" peptide pitched for testosterone support, with no human evidence behind it.
lead: Testagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the sequence Lys-Glu-Asp-Gly (KEDG), part of the family of short "bioregulator" peptides associated with Vladimir Khavinson's group in Russia . It is promoted in research-peptide and longevity communities as supporting testicular function and testosterone.

name: Thymulin
summary: A zinc-dependent thymic peptide hormone; human data cover zinc status, not use as a supplement or for looks.
lead: Thymulin, also called facteur thymique sérique (FTS) or serum thymic factor, is a nine-amino-acid peptide (pGlu-Ala-Lys-Ser-Gln-Gly-Gly-Ser-Asn) produced by the thymus and requiring zinc for biological activity . It was described by Jean-Francois Bach and colleagues in 1977 .

name: Thymosin Beta-4
summary: A natural actin-binding peptide with wound and eye trials and mouse hair data; sold as TB-500, banned in sport.
lead: Thymosin beta-4 (Tβ4) is a small, abundant peptide of about 43 amino acids, encoded by the TMSB4X gene, whose best-established role is binding monomeric actin and thereby regulating the cell cytoskeleton . It was first isolated from calf thymus and sequenced in 1981 by the group of Allan Goldstein .

name: Thymosin Fraction 5
summary: The calf-thymus extract that thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 were purified from; relevant here only as their source.
lead: Thymosin fraction 5 (TF5) is a partially purified extract of calf thymus prepared in 1972 by Allan Goldstein's group, which contains many small peptides, including the later-characterized thymosin alpha-1 and thymosin beta-4 . It was the starting material from which individual thymosins were purified.

name: Thymopentin
summary: A thymus-derived immune peptide studied for infections and skin disease, with no appearance trials behind it.
lead: Thymopentin (also abbreviated TP5) is a synthetic pentapeptide made of the amino acids arginine, lysine, aspartate, valine and tyrosine, derived from the thymus hormone thymopoietin. It is classed as an immunostimulant (ATC code L03AX09) and is described as interacting with T cells.

name: GHRP-3
summary: A little-studied growth hormone-releasing peptide known mainly from anti-doping lists.
lead: GHRP-3 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP), one of a numbered series of small peptides that act on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor to stimulate growth hormone release. It is listed by name among the peptides prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency.

name: GHRP-4
summary: An obscure GH-releasing peptide that shows up in anti-doping papers and nowhere in human trials.
lead: GHRP-4 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide in the numbered GHRP series. Analytical papers describe the GHRPs as synthetic met-enkephalin analogues containing unnatural D-amino acids, designed to stimulate growth hormone release. The family is described as orally active and capable of raising endogenous growth hormone.

name: GHRP-5
summary: The "Momany peptide": a GH-releasing peptide with lab and anti-doping papers but no human trials.
lead: GHRP-5 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide, also referred to in the literature as the Momany peptide. Analytical papers group it with GHRP-1, -2, -4 and -6 as synthetic met-enkephalin analogues with unnatural D-amino acids designed to stimulate growth hormone release.

name: Livoletide
summary: An investigational unacylated-ghrelin peptide built for Prader-Willi hunger, with its pivotal trial terminated.
lead: Livoletide (AZP-531) is a cyclic peptide analogue of unacylated ghrelin that was developed to treat hyperphagia, the intense and persistent hunger, in Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS). Its appearance-related interest stems from its status as an experimental appetite and body-weight drug.

name: Lenomorelin (Ghrelin)
summary: The stomach hunger hormone and GH secretagogue; central to appetite science, untested for looks.
lead: Ghrelin, whose international nonproprietary name is lenomorelin, is a peptide hormone made mainly by enteroendocrine cells of the stomach. It is widely called the "hunger hormone" because it raises the drive to eat, and it also stimulates growth hormone release from the pituitary, which gave it its name.

name: Cortistatin-14
summary: A somatostatin-related brain peptide that also binds ghrelin-type receptors; basic science only, nothing on looks.
lead: Cortistatin-14 is a naturally occurring neuropeptide related to somatostatin. It was named for its predominantly cortical expression and its ability to depress cortical activity, and it shares 11 of its 14 amino acids with somatostatin-14 even though the two peptides are encoded by separate genes .

name: LUM-201
summary: An oral GH-secretagogue (ibutamoren) in trials for children with GH deficiency; nothing tests it for looks.
lead: LUM-201 (ibutamoren, formerly MK-0677) is an orally administered growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist under clinical development for pediatric growth hormone deficiency (PGHD) . It is developed as a daily oral alternative to injected growth hormone.

name: IGF-1 DES
summary: A truncated IGF-1 analogue forum users inject locally for jaw and muscle growth; only cell and animal data exist.
lead: IGF-1 DES, written des(1-3)IGF-1, is a truncated form of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) lacking the first three amino acids at the N-terminus. The truncation lowers its affinity for IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), and in laboratory assays it was more potent than full-length IGF-1 at stimulating protein synthesis in rat muscle cells .
claims: Injecting IGF-1 DES locally can grow the chin, mandible and neck
Combining growth hormone with IGF-1 DES could help a teenager reach genetic height potential
Transdermal androgens plus IGF-1 DES form an effective facial remodelling stack

name: Somatrogon
summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone for children with diagnosed GH deficiency; no evidence for height gain without a deficiency.
lead: Somatrogon (MOD-4023; brand name Ngenla) is a long-acting recombinant human growth hormone analogue given by subcutaneous injection once a week. In the United States it is indicated for children aged 3 years and older with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone .

name: Lonapegsomatropin
summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone prodrug for children and adults with diagnosed GH deficiency; no data for height without deficiency.
lead: Lonapegsomatropin (brand name Skytrofa; development name TransCon hGH) is a once-weekly, long-acting prodrug of growth hormone given by subcutaneous injection. The US FDA approved it in August 2021 for pediatric growth hormone deficiency (GHD) .

name: Somapacitan
summary: A weekly albumin-binding growth hormone for diagnosed GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions; no data for height otherwise.
lead: Somapacitan (brand name Sogroya) is a once-weekly growth hormone derivative that binds reversibly to albumin, given by subcutaneous injection . The US label covers pediatric patients aged 2.5 years and older with growth hormone deficiency (GHD), short stature born small for gestational age, Noonan syndrome growth failure and idiopathic short stature, as well as adults with GHD .

name: Mecasermin
summary: Prescription recombinant IGF-1 for rare severe IGF-1 deficiency in children; talked about for height but only studied in that narrow group.
lead: Mecasermin, sold as Increlex, is a recombinant form of human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) made in E. coli and given by subcutaneous injection.  The US label indicates it for growth failure in children aged 2 and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, or with growth hormone (GH) gene deletion who have developed neutralizing antibodies to GH.
